feature: A highlight offers one line round it, once
summary: Picking a highlight used to put two rows called Outline one above the other, painting different colours, with nothing on screen to say which was which. A highlight now shows Color for the wash it paints and one Outline for the ring round it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: New blank canvas. Press the highlighter tool in the tool bar.
Drag a highlight across the canvas.
Press V to go back to the pointer, then click the highlight.
Read the Appearance section: it says Color, Outline, Shadow, once each.
Tick Outline. A ring appears round the highlight.
Open the Outline row with its chevron and pull the width. Then untick it: the ring goes, the wash stays.
Draw a rectangle and click it. Fill, Outline and Shadow read the way they always did.

evaluate: Is Color the right word for the wash a highlighter lays down, or would you look for Fill?
Is a ring round a highlight something you would ever switch on, or is that row in the way?
When you tick Outline, should the ring come up in the highlight's own colour rather than black?
Picking a highlight together with a rectangle still shows two rows called Outline, because they are two different colours underneath. Does that bother you enough to fix?
rough: The wash row is called Color rather than Fill on purpose: pick a highlight together with a rectangle and a row called Fill would appear twice, which is the problem this task was about.

The mixed selection case is untouched. A rectangle picked with a picture, or with a highlight, still shows an Outline for the shape's own stroke and another for the ring, because one row can only point at one colour today. Filed as its own task.
Screen Recording was granted, so both pictures here are real captures of the window, not offscreen renders.
